questions.stem: What is the term used to describe lines that never meet, no matter how far they are extended?
questions.solution: The term used to describe lines that never meet, no matter how far they are extended, is 'parallel lines'. These lines remain the same distance apart at all points. Perpendicular lines meet at right angles, intersecting lines cross each other at a point, and transversal lines cut across two or more other lines.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about parallel lines is true?
questions.solution: Parallel lines are defined as lines that never meet, no matter how far they are extended. The statement that they intersect at one point or two points is incorrect because parallel lines, by definition, do not intersect. Additionally, lines with different slopes are not parallel, as parallel lines must have the same slope.

questions.stem: In Fig. 5.14, if ∠1 is 60°, which of the following angles must also be 60°?
questions.solution: In Fig. 5.14, if ∠1 is 60°, then ∠5, which is a corresponding angle, must also be 60°. This is because corresponding angles formed by a transversal intersecting two parallel lines are equal. ∠2 is supplementary to ∠1, ∠3 is vertically opposite to ∠1, and ∠4 is supplementary to ∠3.

questions.stem: If two lines are parallel, what can be said about their slopes?
questions.solution: If two lines are parallel, they never intersect, which in coordinate geometry means they have the same steepness, or slope. Therefore, their slopes must be equal. Negative reciprocals would mean the lines are perpendicular, zero slope indicates a horizontal line, and undefined slope indicates a vertical line, none of which apply to parallel lines.

questions.stem: In the given figure, if line l is parallel to line m and line n is a transversal intersecting them at points A and B, and if ∠1 = 110°, what is the measure of ∠2?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 70°. Since line l is parallel to line m and line n is a transversal, ∠1 and ∠2 are supplementary angles (they form a linear pair). Therefore, ∠2 = 180° - ∠1 = 180° - 110° = 70°. The other options are incorrect because 110° would be the measure of an alternate interior angle, 180° would be the sum of the two angles, and 90° is not related to the given angles in this scenario.

hi.stem: दिए गए चित्र में, यदि रेखा l रेखा m के समांतर है और रेखा n उन्हें बिंदु A और B पर काटती है, और यदि ∠1 = 110°, तो ∠2 का माप क्या है?
hi.solution: सही उत्तर 70° है। चूंकि रेखा l रेखा m के समांतर है और रेखा n एक तिर्यक रेखा है, ∠1 और ∠2 संपूरक कोण हैं (वे एक रैखिक युग्म बनाते हैं)। इसलिए, ∠2 = 180° - ∠1 = 180° - 110° = 70°। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि 110° एक वैकल्पिक आंतरिक कोण का माप होता, 180° दोनों कोणों के योग के रूप में होता, और 90° इस परिदृश्य में दिए गए कोणों से संबंधित नहीं होता।

mr.solution: बरोबर उत्तर 70° आहे. रेख l रेख m ला समांतर असल्याने आणि रेख n ही छेदिका असल्याने, ∠1 आणि ∠2 हे एकरूप कोन आहेत (ते एक रेषीय जोडी बनवतात). म्हणून, ∠2 = 180° - ∠1 = 180° - 110° = 70°. इतर उत्तरे अयोग्य आहेत कारण 110° हे विरुद्ध आंतरिक कोनाचे माप असेल, 180° हे दोन कोनांच्या बेरजेचे माप असेल आणि 90° हा दिलेल्या कोनांशी संबंधित नसेल.

questions.stem: If two lines intersect at a point and the sum of two adjacent angles formed is 180°, what can be concluded?
questions.solution: When two lines intersect, the adjacent angles formed are supplementary, meaning they add up to 180°. This is a fundamental geometric property of intersecting lines. The correct answer is that the lines are intersecting, as this is the only scenario where such angles can be formed. Perpendicular lines form 90° angles, parallel lines do not intersect, and coincident lines overlap entirely, none of which apply here.

hi.stem: यदि दो रेखाएं एक बिंदु पर प्रतिच्छेद करती हैं और बने दो संलग्न कोणों का योग 180° है, तो क्या निष्कर्ष निकाला जा सकता है?
